paper.title_en: Two Higgs Doublet Model from Six-Dimensional Gauge Theory
paper.abstract_en: We investigate a two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) based on a six-dimensional $SU(4)$ gauge theory compactified on $T^2/Z_2$. The six-dimensional gauge symmetry ensures that the tree-level Higgs potential is CP conserving and $Z_2$ symmetric, while the Yukawa interactions of bulk fermions are naturally aligned, suppressing tree-level flavor-changing neutral currents. The $SU(4)$ charge embedding accommodates the quark electric charges, while the group-theoretical enhancement of the Yukawa coupling in the sixth-rank totally symmetric representation leads to the tree level relation $m_t\simeq 2m_W$. We show that electroweak symmetry breaking can be realized and the observed SM Higgs boson mass can be reproduced through appropriate choices of the brane-localized gauge kinetic term coefficient and the bulk matter content. We also obtain predictions for the masses of the additional Higgs bosons. Furthermore, we show that the torus geometry affects both the Higgs mass spectrum and the couplings of the CP-even Higgs bosons to electroweak gauge bosons. Finally, we identify parameter regions in which the additional Higgs mass spectra are consistent with the ATLAS and CMS measurements of the W-boson mass within the approximation based on the scalar-sector contribution to $Δρ$.
